hypotheses.claim: If `score_item` is a lexicographic priority: (a) size descending as the base term, plus (b) a bounded deterministic tie-break term derived from a cheap residual-fit heuristic (e.g. item size modulo the dominant bin-fill quantum, or hash(size) so equal-size items are ordered consistently yet differently across bins), then the reorder-repack loop will close part of the ~2.4-2.7% relative gap on size 50/100 instances without regressing size 200, because FFD orderings tie on large items and the residual term drives the small-item placement that determines whether the last bin is needed.

next_search_advice.direction: Refine the offline `score_item` priority to break the 2-3% gap on the small/medium instances: prioritize large items (size descending) but perturb ties with a deterministic hashed jitter so that FFD-like packing explores alternative insertion orders, and let the repack pass relocate the smallest items of under-filled bins. Push toward reducing bin count on size=50 (13.0 mean) and size=100 (24.25 mean) regimes.
